lane: tectonic geomorphology: channel steepness (chi / ksn) and knickpoints, not scarp shape
hypothesis: Chi/ksn steepness steps corroborated across >= 3 independent drainages along a common strike mark fault traces that the GIVEN Quaternary catalogue omits. Because the competition's hidden truth is off-catalogue, the lane's mandated first test must be run against off-catalogue fault segments, not against withheld catalogue segments.
mechanism: A fault offsets base level; the steepness contrast propagates upstream as a knickpoint (Kirby & Whipple 2012, J. Struct. Geol. 44, 54-75, doi:10.1016/j.jsg.2012.07.009; Perron & Royden 2013, ESPL 38, 570-576, doi:10.1002/esp.3302; Gailleton et al. 2019, ESurf 7, 211-230, doi:10.5194/esurf-7-211-2019). Single-channel steps are ambiguous; strike-aligned corroboration across drainage divides is not, because no single-channel process is strike-aligned.
mimicking_non_fault_process: Lithologic contacts and basin-fill boundaries (a hard-over-weak contact also steps ksn and can be strike-aligned), alluvial fan-apex and fan-head trenching steps, playa / pluvial-shoreline base levels, channel-head and colluvial-to-fluvial transitions near the A_ch threshold, and SGMC mapping of old, inactive or poorly located traces.
substrate: USGS 3DEP 1/3 arc-second (~10 m) DEM, 18 current 1x1-degree tiles, public domain
budget_note: 3 experiments declared; 4 measurement rounds were run because the first emission FAILED the uniqueness gate (75.7% of its dots within 3 px of the H65-1 file) and had to be re-emitted on a different limb of the same statistic. Logged rather than hidden.
